The tool is part of the RAND Budget Model Initiative, which helps show how federal policy decisions will impact real people, real businesses, and real communities. ⬇️
bit.ly/3Qb7KSC

A few key takeaways:

🔸There are more than three dozen deductions, credits, and other adjustments to consider when assessing an individual's tax liability.
🔸Sections of the tax code that affect corporations contain more than triple the credits and deductions of individual income tax sections, but they bring in one-tenth of the revenue.
🔸Making the tax code more complex can actually reduce tax receipts.
There's much more to explore here: rand.org/pubs/research_brief…

The corporate part of the tax code is substantially more complex than the part for individuals, with about twice as many regulations and sections.

Here's the flow of corporate tax money, with different types of potentially taxable income entering the graph from the left (in green). Deductions flow off the top, eventually leaving the total tax revenue (in yellow).

Our tool helps map the flow of money through the entire tax system.

For individual tax returns, different types of potentially taxable income enter the graph from the left (in green), flow off in adjustments and deductions, and leave the total amount of taxes generated (in blue).

💸 Today is Tax Day.

America's tax system raises trillions in revenue to fuel the government, but the text itself is a labyrinth. That makes it hard to understand the true effects of any proposed changes to the tax code. Even small "fixes" can cause ripple effects and unintended consequences.

How to make sense of this? RAND researchers developed an innovative new tool to disentangle the tax code and help policymakers better understand these effects.
